script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: career transition

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Forty-something MARY, a stressed-out and successful marketing executive, sits on her worn-out couch, staring at her phone. She bites her lower lip, her eyes glued to the screen.

MARY
(Aloud)
Come on. Come on. You can do this.

Her phone rings. She looks up, expecting it to be her boss. Instead, it's her sister, LIZ.

LIZ (V.O.)
Hey, Mary. How's it going?

INT. KITCHEN - DAY

Mary's sister, Liz, a free-spirited artist, paints in her sunlit kitchen. She sips her tea, waiting for Mary to answer.

MARY
(V.O.)
Same old. Another all-nighter.

LIZ
(V.O.)
Mary, you need a break. Have you thought about quitting your job and pursuing your passion?

INT. MARY'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Mary stands in her dimly lit bedroom, looking at her collection of old, unused paintings. She remembers her childhood dreams of becoming an artist.

MARY
(Aloud)
What if I can't make it? What if I fail?

INT. GALLERY - DAY

Mary visits a local art gallery, taking in the vibrant colors and inspiring works of art. She overhears a conversation between an artist and a gallery owner.

ARTIST
I've been struggling to sell my pieces. I'm thinking of giving up.

GALLERY OWNER
(Encouragingly)
Don't give up. Persistence pays off. Keep creating and putting yourself out there.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Mary sits at her kitchen table, surrounded by her old paintings, her face filled with determination.

MARY
I can do this.

INT. ART CLASS - DAY

Mary attends her first art class, her hands trembling as she holds her paintbrush. She feels out of place, surrounded by younger, more experienced artists.

INSTRUCTOR
Welcome, Mary. I'm glad to see a new face. Today, we'll be working on portraits.

Mary looks nervous but determined.

MARY
I'm ready.

INT. LIVING ROOM - EVENING

Mary arrives home from her art class, her canvas covered in paint. She looks at her reflection in the mirror, a smile forming on her lips.

MARY
I'm an artist.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Mary sits in a coffee shop, her laptop open in front of her, writing a proposal for a local art exhibition. She feels a sense of pride and fulfillment.

INT. GALLERY - NIGHT

Mary stands in front of her artwork, displayed at the exhibition. She watches as people admire her creations, their eyes filled with wonder and appreciation.

MARY
I made it.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Mary sits on her couch, her phone ringing. It's her boss.

BOSS (V.O.)
Mary, I need you to come in tonight.

Mary looks conflicted but then makes a decision.

MARY
(Aloud)
I can't. I've quit.

MARY smiles, feeling free and alive for the first time in years.

FADE OUT.

THE END
